sources.author: Russell K.Engelman2022, BMC Biology20:37
sources.evidence: Read relevant introduction/caption, actually viewed original Fig1B H.horridus reconstructed skeleton after Scott and Jepsen; same thorax-length normalization not body scale. Relatively big head, long tail, comparatively short limbs.

sources.title: Tooth puncture marks on a30million year old Dinictis skull
sources.author: John W.Hoganson and Jeff J.Person2011, North Dakota Geological Survey GeoNews
sources.evidence: Relevant discussion read; original Fig8 actual Hyaenodon skull and Table2 inspected. Caption25cm skull; SDSM493 canine spacing35.4mm and SDSM3017 spacing40.2mm; latter leftcanine15.1x10.8mm AP/LL. Caption lacks explicit specimenID, so retain separation. Long jaws/cheek teeth and slightly compressed canines.
sources.rights: NDGS authors; private research reference, no image embedded in public output.
